Laura / Marcus — looping you in to review Anna's redlines and the TIA. Quick context: HealthPrism is EU-headquartered, will sign Redwood MSA + Order Form, and needs SCCs + a TIA because they use CloudZone (US) as a subprocessor.

On Thu, 03 Dec 2027 at 16:20:00 +0000, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HealthPrism - DPA + SCCs: order form alignment and TIA

Monica / Marcus — I reviewed the redline and the TIA. High level: we can accept the controller-processor SCCs, subject to two clarifications and one addendum.

1) Subprocessor coverage: the redline needs an explicit subprocessor table tied to Exhibit B (we should provide a template row). The contract should require Redwood to maintain an up-to-date list and 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; HealthPrism's redline asked for prior written consent for all subprocessors which we should push back on — we can offer prior notice + objection for high-risk subprocessors only.

Suggested clause (language we should propose back):
"Redwood will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors (Exhibit B). Redwood shall provide written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to the onboarding of any new subprocessor and shall allow Customer to object on reasonable security grounds to any high-risk subprocessor within such notice period. If no objection is raised within thirty (30) days, Redwood may engage the subprocessor."

2) SCC variant: use Controller-Processor (Module Two-style), with Tailored clauses consistent with EU Commission guidance. We need to confirm whether HealthPrism prefers the standalone SCCs or integrated SCCs in the DPA; recommend standalone Annex with explicit cross-reference in the MSA.

3) TIA notes: the TIA flags the CloudZone US data center. Operational mitigations are adequate (encryption at rest/in transit, limited personnel access), but we should propose the Transfer Impact Addendum language that documents those mitigations and references our internal audit report (we can provide a redacted summary).

Action items for Marcus: please draft a Schedule A mapping for data categories + retention buckets and add an Exhibit B template for subprocessors. I can provide the legal text for the SCCs and the TIA addendum.

I will also flag that HealthPrism's redline included an unusually broad audit right. We should accept on a scoped basis (annual audits or SOC reports + targeted on-site with notice). I'll propose language.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Contracting & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Kovacs <anna.kovacs@healthprism.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2027 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HealthPrism - DPA + SCCs: order form alignment and TIA - final steps

Thanks Laura — good notes. Monica / Anna — I'm attaching a first-pass Schedule A (data-mapping.xlsx) and an Exhibit B subprocessors template in the drive link (see related links). Key points I implemented: 

- Schedule A: mapped HealthPrism's listed categories to Order Form line items (PII, Provider Data, Usage Telemetry). Retention buckets added (30/90/365 days + custom retention cap for backups).
- Exhibit B: includes CloudZone with hosting location (us-east-1) and a redbox indicator for high-risk flagging workflow.
- Audit: scoped to SOC2 or equivalent reports annually; on-site audits by exception with 60 days' notice and cost allocation clause.

Next steps:
1) Laura to provide SCCs + TIA addendum legal text by EOD Monday.
2) Monica to send updated doc bundle + DocuSign envelope to HealthPrism for signature once legal text is inserted.
3) Anna: can you confirm whether HealthPrism needs the integrated SCC variant or prefers standalone annex? If integrated, we will add cross-references in the MSA and Order Form.

Target: execute by 2027-12-10 to meet Q4 procurement timelines.
